A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RSD research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v3 reports original RSD evaluations and ablations, including Tables 1–6 and the higher-resolution training experiment in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds benchmark evaluations, I2SB/IBMD experiments, training-cost measurements and stability analyses.

M1.justification: The RSD architecture, distillation objective, auxiliary fake model, LPIPS/GAN losses, multistep training and single-step inference remain unchanged (Section 3; Algorithm 1). Added experiments vary existing settings without replacing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v4 adds full-size RealLR200 and RealLQ250 evaluations (Table 14), extending real-world image coverage within the existing 4× blind super-resolution task. Previous real and synthetic benchmarks, including ImageNet and LSDIR training coverage, remain.

E2.justification: v4 adds CTMSR, AdcSR, PiSA-SR, TSD-SR, InvSR and CCSR to corresponding benchmark comparisons, plus an I2SB/IBMD comparison in Appendix A.3. Existing comparisons, including ResShift-VSD and AddSR, are retained.

E3.justification: v4 adds FID evaluation, new I2SB/IBMD training budgets and NFE configurations, and a matched four-A100 training-cost experiment including teacher training (Table 18). These expand the evaluation design; the original RSD training and benchmark protocols remain.

E4.justification: New Appendix F tests fake-model update counts K = 1, 3, 5 and 10 with and without supervised losses, adding convergence curves and visual loss-effect analyses. Appendix E adds failure-case comparisons with recent methods. Earlier timestep, supervised-loss and higher-resolution studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-seed counts, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. The new convergence plots compare training configurations without adding statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous comparator, benchmark, FID, IBMD, ablation and timing results are added while original core RSD scores remain. Rankings change: under the retained A100 timing setup, v4 Table 4 reports AdcSR at 0.024 seconds versus RSD's unchanged 0.059 seconds, which was previously fastest.

T1.justification: Appendices A.2–A.3 correct minimization to maximization in equivalent RSD loss reformulations (v4 Equations 31–32) and drop v3's final nested-minimization expression. The main objective, Proposition 3.1 and its proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v4 qualifies teacher superiority by named perceptual metrics and shifts headline emphasis from better input alignment toward quality under limited training and inference costs. Section 1 adds an explicit superiority claim over IBMD while retaining the central one-step ResShift distillation contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of supervised losses stabilizing small-K training, CTMSR blur potentially arising from deterministic consistency training, and resolution trade-offs reflecting teacher behavior (Appendices E–G). It also acknowledges that PiSA-SR and TSD-SR generally achieve better perceptual quality, developing the quality-versus-compute interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendices A.3 and C–E substantially expand reproduction information through comparator checkpoint filenames, code and weight links, dataset sources and licenses, and training instructions and resource budgets. v4 also explicitly identifies the standard teacher checkpoint and its 300k training iterations; existing RSD hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix E substantially expand positioning against recent consistency-based and T2I-based SR methods, including CTMSR, AdcSR, PiSA-SR and InvSR. Appendix A.3 develops the existing IBMD relationship into a detailed practical comparison, alongside substantive citation additions.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and method explanations are extensively rewritten and condensed, with reorganized contributions and discussion. v4 adds an appendix roadmap, inserts substantial appendix sections and moves the societal-impact statement into the main text.

P2.justification: v4 adopts two-column main text, restructures tables with model/T2I groupings, FID columns and training-cost rows, and adds comparison and ablation displays. Figure 3 is recomposed with new comparators, while older qualitative galleries are shortened and redistributed.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens the quality-efficiency argument through contemporary competitors, teacher-inclusive matched timing measurements (Table 18), and training-stability evidence (Appendix F), resolving important gaps in v3's empirical support. It also corrects optimization formulas and qualifies headline claims. The IBMD comparison still uses different teachers and architectures, limiting attribution specifically to the loss, but the additional controlled analyses provide a substantial net quality gain.
